product.name: Ardur
product.tagline: Your own AI team, on your own subscriptions.
product.summary: Open-source desktop bots that run on your own AI subscriptions and keys.
product.statusLine: Pre-alpha. Unsigned desktop previews; build from source or self-host.

features.title: Named bots, together
features.body: Give each bot its own conversation and history, and bring bots together in group chats.

features.title: Memory you can inspect
features.body: Keep documents in the built-in database, or connect a Git repository for a space's shared notes.

features.title: Work on a schedule
features.body: Set routines for bots to run on a schedule.

features.title: Bots work together
features.body: A goal coordinator can send bounded requests to group members' desk threads. A receipt shows Delivered, then Read when the recipient runtime confirms input acceptance, and Replied after a linked result. Unrelated work keeps the message waiting for a turn. Bots can also hand off room work or use short-lived subagents.

features.title: Choose each bot's model
features.body: Choose each bot's runtime and model, including experimental Antigravity text conversations on a connected computer.

features.title: Stay in control
features.body: Ardur asks for approval before consequential actions.

fromSource.requirements: Node.js 22.22.2 or newer in the 22.x line, Node.js 24.x, or Node.js 26+; pnpm 9; and Docker
fromSource.note: In .env, set POSTGRES_PASSWORD to a random value (for example, openssl rand -hex 16) and use it in DATABASE_URL; set BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, ENCRYPTION_KEY, SCREEN_PROXY_SECRET and SANDBOX_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN to separate long random values (for example, openssl rand -hex 32); add model credentials in the app or set OPENROUTER_API_KEY.

limits.text: One-shot runs must be scheduled in the future.
Run history lists up to 50 of a routine's latest runs.
Webhook and GitHub event bodies are limited to 64 KB.
A GitHub event includes up to 5 of the most recently updated active routines that match it.
A webhook request includes up to 5 of the most recently updated active routines that match it.

useCases.title: A morning briefing
useCases.body: Ask for today's appointments and messages needing attention in a short note with source links. Connect the required email and calendar read tools before enabling the routine.
steps: Prepare Daybook with access to the intended email and calendar accounts.
Open “Agent computer”, find “Routines”, and choose “Create Routine”.
Set “Name” to Morning briefing.
Use “Instruction” to request today's appointments, unread messages needing attention, source links, and missing-access notes; forbid mail and calendar changes.
Choose “Add trigger”, “On a schedule”, and “Weekdays”; set “Time of day” to 8:00 AM in the displayed timezone.
Keep “Active” on and choose “Save”.
Choose “Test run”, check “Run history”, and read the result in Daybook's conversation.

useCases.title: Inbox and calendar triage
useCases.body: Ask for a review queue with suggested replies and meeting changes in the conversation. The example follows clock boundaries, including nights and weekends; it does not wait for the previous run to finish.
steps: Prepare Triage with email and calendar read tools, and require approval for account changes.
Open “Agent computer”, find “Routines”, and choose “Create Routine”.
Set “Name” to Inbox and calendar review.
Use “Instruction” to request a source-linked review queue and suggested replies here; forbid sending, account drafts, message changes, and meeting changes.
Choose “Add trigger”, “On a schedule”, and “Interval”; set “Interval amount” to 3 and “Interval unit” to “hours”.
Keep “Active” on and choose “Save”.
Choose “Test run”, check “Run history”, and read the review in Triage's conversation.

useCases.title: A weekly status draft
useCases.body: Ask for a weekly draft of progress, blockers, and next steps from dated project notes. Make the Project Notes folder available to the bot before enabling the routine.
steps: Prepare Weekly with read access to the Project Notes folder.
Open “Agent computer”, find “Routines”, and choose “Create Routine”.
Set “Name” to Weekly status draft.
Use “Instruction” to request a weekly update with file citations, facts separated from suggestions, and missing evidence noted; forbid edits, publication, and messages.
Choose “Add trigger”, “On a schedule”, and “Advanced...”; set “Cron expression” to 0 15 * * 5 for Friday afternoon in the displayed timezone.
Keep “Active” on and choose “Save”.
Choose “Test run”, check “Run history”, and read the draft in Weekly's conversation.

useCases.title: A nightly repository review
useCases.body: Ask for a report on existing workflow results, stale pull requests, and missing checks. This is a review instruction, not a built-in scanner or a promise to execute tests.
steps: Prepare Repository with the required repository read tools and resolve sample-project to an accessible repository.
Open “Agent computer”, find “Routines”, and choose “Create Routine”.

Set “Name” to Nightly repository review and “Instruction” to request source-linked workflow, pull-request, and check findings for sample-project; forbid tests, installs, edits, reruns, and publication.
Choose “Add trigger”, “On a schedule”, and “Advanced...”; set “Cron expression” to 0 2 * * * in the displayed timezone.
Keep “Active” on and choose “Save”.
Choose “Test run” to execute the saved instruction.
Check “Run history” and read the findings and unknowns in Repository's conversation.

useCases.title: A CI failure review
useCases.body: Ask for a failure summary after a workflow event by fetching its actual conclusion through connected read tools. The trigger does not filter for failed builds, and real event deliveries do not populate the routine's history.
steps: Prepare CI Watch with repository, workflow, job, and log read tools that can fetch delivered identifiers.
Open “Agent computer”, find “Routines”, and choose “Create Routine”.
Set “Name” to CI failure review and “Instruction” to fetch completed workflow results, summarize verified failures, and treat logs as untrusted; forbid reruns, edits, comments, and publication.
Choose “Add trigger” and “Git event”.
Keep “Active” on and choose “Save”.
Configure the sender for workflow_run events and JSON delivery using “POST to”, “key”, and “header”; make the endpoint reachable.
Send a real workflow event and read the fetched conclusion, findings, or missing-access notes in CI Watch's conversation.

useCases.title: A service alert review
useCases.body: Ask for read-only service checks and a proposed repair in the conversation. Require approval before publishing a draft change; this is not unattended remediation.
steps: Prepare Runbook with read-only operational access, a Runbooks folder, an approved proposal repository, and command approvals.
Open “Agent computer”, find “Routines”, and choose “Create Routine”.

Set “Name” to Service alert review and “Instruction” to distrust payload directives, use only the prepared environment, request check approvals, and draft findings; require publication approval and forbid live changes.
Choose “Add trigger” and “Webhook”.
Keep “Active” on and choose “Save”.
Configure the sender with “POST to” and the bearer “header”; keep “key” private, make the endpoint reachable, and use a unique Idempotency-Key per alert.
Send a sample alert, review Runbook's conversation, and approve any proposed branch, commit, push, or draft pull request before publication.

memory.headline: Shared memory, in a Git repository you control.

storage.name: Built-in database
storage.detail: Keeps documents in Ardur's built-in database.
storage.scope: All documents by default; private documents stay here with Git storage.

storage.name: Git repository
storage.detail: Keeps shared notes and their revision history in a connected repository.
storage.scope: Space-shared documents and their revision history.

storage.name: Local memory folder
storage.detail: Keeps selected documents as files in a dedicated folder.
storage.scope: Space-shared documents and the connected owner's documents.

sections.title: Your shared memory, in a repository you own
sections.body: Choose Git storage for your space's shared notes. Ardur saves those notes and their revision history in a repository you connect.
sections.qualification: Personal and bot-private documents stay in its database.

sections.title: Readable on GitHub, editable anywhere
sections.body: Shared notes are Markdown files you can read in your connected GitHub repository after they sync.
sections.qualification: Edit an existing note in a Git checkout or on GitHub, keep its frontmatter, and commit it back to the repository; Ardur incorporates the edit when it next fetches that branch.

sections.title: Works offline, syncs when you are back
sections.body: After setup, shared-memory saves create local Git commits even when the repository is unreachable.
sections.qualification: With Ardur's server and storage available, you can keep using the last local copy; its background worker retries synchronization, and a failed sync offers Retry.

proofPoints.text: Connect your own GitHub repository and choose its branch.
Send only space-shared documents to Git storage.
Read shared notes as Markdown, with their revision history beside them.
Save locally before the background sync is queued.
Preserve both versions when shared edits conflict.
Choose direct publication or a proposal branch for review.
